title: An LFU Cache

concept.title: Buckets of keys by frequency, each bucket ordered by recency
body: An **LFU** cache removes the **least frequently used** key when it is full; if several keys share the lowest frequency, the **least recently used** of them goes. Each `get` or `put` of a key counts as one use. All operations must be O(1).

Keep three things: `value[key]`, `freq[key]`, and for every frequency `f` an **ordered set of keys** with that frequency, ordered by recency (the oldest first). Also keep `min_freq`, the lowest frequency that exists. To **touch** a key with frequency `f`: remove it from the bucket `f` (if the bucket becomes empty and `f == min_freq`, then `min_freq` becomes `f + 1`), and append it to the bucket `f + 1`. To **evict**, remove the first key of the bucket `min_freq`. A new key starts with frequency 1, so `min_freq` is 1 after inserting it.

body.code:
touch(key): f = freq[key]; del buckets[f][key]
            if not buckets[f]: del buckets[f]; if min_freq == f: min_freq += 1
            freq[key] = f + 1; buckets[f + 1][key] = None      # appended: most recent
evict:      key = first key of buckets[min_freq]; remove it everywhere

body: Python dictionaries keep the insertion order, so a `dict` works as the ordered set. In Java use `LinkedHashSet`, in C++ a `list` with a map of iterators.

statement: Implement an LFU cache with the capacity `cap`. Process `n` operations (each line has an operation and two numbers). `get key 0` prints the value of the key, or -1 if it is not in the cache; a successful `get` counts as a use of the key. `put key value` stores the value; if the key exists, its value is replaced and this counts as a use; if the key is new and the cache is full, the key with the smallest number of uses is removed first (among such keys the one that was used longest ago). A new key has one use. Print the answer of every `get`.
inputFormat: Each of the next `n` lines has an operation and two numbers.
constraints: There is at least one `get` operation.

examples.input:
9 2
put 1 1
put 2 2
get 1 0
put 3 3
get 2 0
get 3 0
put 4 4
get 1 0
get 3 0
examples.note: Key 1 has two uses, key 2 has one: put 3 removes key 2, so get 2 gives -1. After get 3, keys 1 and 3 both have two uses; put 4 removes key 1, the one used longer ago: get 1 gives -1 and get 3 gives 3.

hints: Keep, for every frequency, the keys with this frequency in order of use.
Remember the smallest frequency in the cache.
When a key is used, move it from its frequency bucket to the next one; evict from the bucket of the smallest frequency, taking its oldest key.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, cap = map(int, input().split())
ops = [input().split() for _ in range(n)]

# Your code here

explanation: Keys are grouped by frequency in ordered buckets. A use moves a key to the next bucket, and eviction takes the oldest key of the bucket with the smallest frequency.
solution.complexity: O(1) per operation on average, space O(cap).
